elevator_pitch: A decision-support simulator that helps school learning-support teams test accommodation policies across synthetic learner profiles before rollout.
project_story:
## The problem

School support teams often debate accommodations using an imagined average learner. When a policy removes one relief channel, its effect can change sharply with sensitivity, activation cost, and available alternatives. The assumptions are rarely visible in the meeting record.

## The product

PolicyPilot lets a learning-support team shape a synthetic learner profile, choose an available-channel policy, and run a 14-day trajectory. It reports mean load, peak load, high-load days, a reachable next channel, and the equation behind the result. A counterfactual profile runs under the same policy so the team can see where a one-size-fits-all decision breaks.

## How it is built

The prototype is a browser-local HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript application based on the Pressure-Relief Model. Each simulated day updates unresolved load from pressure, profile-specific sensitivity, reachable relief, activation cost, and natural decay. The model receipt exposes the equation and the counterfactual bars. Scenario export is local JSON with `external_data` set to `false`.

## Who pays and why

The first customers are international schools and small learning-support teams. A paid school pilot would add team workspaces, versioned policy receipts, and an auditable export for student-support meetings. The wedge is not another student label; it is a faster way to test a policy assumption before it affects a real learner.

## What is next

The next build would validate the six model dimensions with learning-support staff, add teacher-authored policy templates, and measure whether the receipt improves the quality of accommodation discussions. The research parameters require empirical validation before operational use.

## Responsible boundary

PolicyPilot uses synthetic trajectories. It is not a mental-health assessment, risk score, diagnosis, or treatment recommender, and it does not upload student data.

## AI-use disclosure

AI coding assistance was used for brainstorming, implementation drafting, and debugging. The project owner reviewed the implementation and remains responsible for understanding and explaining the code.
